title: Mantle Health — capacity uplift + split-region rollout review
next_steps: Send updated 18-month pricing and amortized per-token example
Share SOC2/ISO pack and KMS/HSM integration notes
Schedule 90-minute end-to-end benchmark for EU region (provision dev cluster)
Draft runbook for split-region rollout and traffic steering (canary)
action_items: Lena Park: send amended contract draft with 18-month term and capacity uplift numbers (due 2026-03-29)
Marcus Hale: prepare benchmark plan + test vectors and coordinate dev cluster (due 2026-04-02)
Owen Patel: share current infra diagram and expected peak qps/latency SLOs (due 2026-03-26)
Sara Kim: list data residency and retention policy items we need in SOC pack (due 2026-03-31)
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-03-24 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park, Marcus Hale, Riley Chen (Redwood) — Dr. Nina Rao, Tom Alvarez, Sara Kim, Owen Patel (Mantle Health)
Type: Renewal/Expansion check-in (capacity + regional onramp)
summary: Redwood AE/SE reviewed Mantle Health's request for a capacity uplift, adding an EU sovereign region and a split-region rollout strategy. Discussed trade-offs between Dedicated vs Private deployment, pilot on-prem appliance for PHI workloads, SOC2 and KMS requirements, and next steps: amended contract, benchmark, and runbook. Customer leaning toward 18-month committed capacity with a pilot in EU and a private component for specific data flows.
topics: Capacity uplift sizing and billing impact
EU sovereign region onboarding and data residency
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Park: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, uh this is the kickoff for the renewal and the planned regional rollout, we're hoping to align on numbers and next steps.
[00:12] Dr. Nina Rao: thanks Lena, quick context — our production model calls have grown 2.6x q/q, and EU traffic is around 28% now, we want lower p99s for patient-facing features.
[00:27] Tom Alvarez: and also we have a compliance requirement to keep certain PHI inside EU. so it's not just latency, it's residency.
[00:40] Marcus Hale: yeah understood; from a serving perspective there are a few levers — dedicated pools in the EU region, or private deployment inside Mantle's VPC/on-prem for the PHI pipeline. both have cost and ops tradeoffs.
[00:54] Owen Patel: can you remind us on the Dedicated footprint? our infra team is worried about egress and cross-region KV cache warm up.
[01:07] Lena Park: Dedicated is Redwood-managed GPU pools, predictable throughput. KV cache warm ups happen on cold starts but we have prefix caching and pre-warm options. for strict residency the Private option gives you customer-managed control.
[01:24] Dr. Nina Rao: hmm, we prob need Private for the PHI flows, but the rest of inference could live in Hosted/Dedicated to save cost. is that hybrid approach straightforward?
[01:38] Marcus Hale: yes, we support hybrid routing — policy-based: route PHI-labeled requests to private nodes, and public traffic to Dedicated EU. there is some complexity around model parity and quantization variants.
[01:51] Tom Alvarez: cost wise, what's the delta? we've been leaning toward a committed uplift but want to understand per-token amortized cost if we do split.
[02:04] Lena Park: we ran two back-of-envelope examples — with an 18-month commitment and expected 2.5x throughput uplift, blended unit price drops ~22% vs month-to-month. we'll send the exact numbers after the call.
[02:18] Sara Kim: security questions — we need SOC2 certs, ISO info, audit log retention guarantees, and KMS/HSM key control. can you integrate with our cloud KMS?
[02:31] Marcus Hale: yes, Redwood Private can integrate with customer KMS via our connector, and we support HSM-backed keys for enclave-like key usage. note: some on-prem pilots require local HSMs and a small agent to handle keys — it's been done before but we should scope it.
[02:48] Owen Patel: any differences in latency p99 between Dedicated eu and Private on prem? we aim for sub-200ms user facing in the EU.
[03:01] Marcus Hale: Private co-located on-prem will generally be lower latency for local users. Dedicated in eu-central should hit ~220-260ms p99 depending on model size and sequence length; with prefix caching and batching tuning we can push down. quantization also helps but needs validation on quality.
[03:18] Dr. Nina Rao: that matches our expectations. we do need a short benchmark run to validate p99 and throughput with our prompts, that's non-negotiable.
[03:30] Lena Park: absolutely — Marcus will lead a benchmark plan, we'll provision a dev cluster in eu-west1 for the test and use your prompts and datasets.
[03:40] Tom Alvarez: timeline question — if we commit to 18 months today, when could we have production EU capacity?
[03:50] Lena Park: with committed capacity order we can schedule capacity in the next provisioning window — typically 4–6 weeks to have Dedicated pools ready, Private takes a bit longer if on-prem install and KMS integration are needed, say 6–10 weeks.
[04:04] Sara Kim: on contract changes, we also need clear SLAs for data deletion and auditability.
[04:11] Lena Park: we can add data retention clauses and enhanced audit log retention as an add-on. we'll include language around data deletion requests.
[04:19] Owen Patel: one operational question — how do we handle model updates and rollouts across the split regions? we want canary first in eu-dedicated then private.
[04:29] Marcus Hale: rollout plan looks like: push new model to staging, run canary in eu-dedicated 5% traffic for 24h, run regression evals, then promote to private after validation. we can automate fallback to previous model if regressions happen.
[04:45] Dr. Nina Rao: great. also curious — is there a way to reuse KV cache between regions or is it per-cluster? cross-region sharing would help warm-ups.
[04:57] Marcus Hale: KV cache is per-runtime instance. cross-region sharing introduces consistency and privacy concerns. we do have pre-warm tooling — snapshot preloads for critical prefixes to simulate warm cache at rollout.
[05:12] Tom Alvarez: about cost, does Redwood offer any tooling to model different batching strategies against our latency SLOs?
[05:19] Marcus Hale: yes, Redwood Optimize provides suggestions and a simulator for batching profiles, showing latency vs cost tradeoffs for token distributions. happy to include your traces in the sim.
[05:30] Lena Park: quick checkpoint — it sounds like Mantle wants: 1) 18-month uplift commitment, 2) hybrid deployment (Dedicated EU + Private for PHI), 3) benchmarks and runbook, 4) contract addenda for data residency. is that accurate?
[05:45] Dr. Nina Rao: yes, that matches.
[05:49] Sara Kim: one more compliance note — SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and RBAC enforcement for audit scope. can you support Okta?
[05:59] Riley Chen: yes Okta SAML/SCIM supported. RBAC roles can be mapped to your groups. we'll include the mapping doc.
[06:08] Owen Patel: we might bring in our networking team — they care about VPC peering, NAT egress charges, and firewall rules. we'll need a network runbook from you.
[06:18] Lena Park: we'll produce a network checklist: peering, allowed ports, cidr ranges, egress considerations.
[06:24] Tom Alvarez: small nit — any feature flags for throttling at route level? we want graceful degradation for non-critical prompts during peak.
[06:33] Marcus Hale: yes per-route throttles and soft-fail fallback to cheaper model variants or last-good-response config.
[06:41] Dr. Nina Rao: okay good. can we also have log-level access for tracing model regression incidents? our ML ops team needs per-request traces for a week at least.
[06:52] Riley Chen: we can surface per-request trace ids and a short-term retention window; extended retention is an add-on.
[07:00] Tom Alvarez: are there any gotchas with the private on-prem agent — e.g., ports, cert rotation, upgrades?
[07:08] Marcus Hale: the agent needs outbound TLS to a control plane endpoint for telemetry, cert rotation is automatic but we can support manual rotation workflows. upgrade can be scheduled; we'll aim for non-disruptive patching windows. there are firewall rules needed, we'll include them in the network runbook.
[07:25] Dr. Nina Rao: good. let's talk about pricing structure quickly — we want amortized per-token + reserved GPU nodes turned into a blended rate, does that fit your standard contract?
[07:36] Lena Park: yes we can provide blended pricing. for the 18-month commitment we'll credit part of the private onboarding fees across months to smooth cashflow. detailed spreadsheet will follow.
[07:48] Owen Patel: for the benchmark, can you support synthetic traffic that mimics our peak diurnal pattern? our bursts are very spiky and short.
[07:58] Marcus Hale: yep, we'll craft a load pattern with your burst profiles, including variable sequence lengths. we'll do a throughput ramp and a p99 p95 report.
[08:08] Tom Alvarez: what's a realistic fallback policy if we lose the eu-dedicated capacity during a big event? do requests go to US and we accept higher latency?
[08:19] Marcus Hale: policy engine can route to next-best region; we also have capacity-tier fallbacks — e.g., smaller quantized model in nearby region; we can configure acceptable latency/SLO violation tolerances.
[08:33] Dr. Nina Rao: I want to make sure fallbacks don't leak PHI — if the PHI flag is set, fallback should not go across borders.
[08:42] Marcus Hale: can do — routing policy will honor residency labels and we can block cross-border fallback for flagged requests.
[08:50] Sara Kim: would prefer explicit allow lists per model/route.
[08:55] Lena Park: noted. we'll include that in the runbook and contract language.
[09:01] Owen Patel: any integration work for our monitoring — we use Datadog; can we get per-route metrics and traces into our dashboards?
[09:09] Marcus Hale: yes Datadog integration supported via event export and custom metrics, plus traces with sampling. we'll produce sample dashboards.
[09:19] Tom Alvarez: ok let's clarify the pilot scope — what would you consider the minimal viable pilot?
[09:25] Marcus Hale: M V P pilot: provision a small dedicated eu cluster (2 nodes), private agent for a single PHI pipeline (non-prod), run three-day stress + regression tests against your prompt sets, verify p99 and failover behavior.
[09:38] Dr. Nina Rao: timeline for that?
[09:40] Marcus Hale: if we start provisioning next week, we can run the pilot in ~3 weeks.
[09:45] Lena Park: action items recap coming at the end here. any blockers on your side?
[09:50] Tom Alvarez: legal wants the contract redlines ahead of exec approval.
[09:53] Lena Park: we'll send redline draft by Monday.
[09:56] Riley Chen: also we'll attach the compliance pack and KMS integration notes.
[10:00] Dr. Nina Rao: perfect. one more question — are there examples of other health customers doing hybrid private+D edicated deployments?
[10:09] Lena Park: yes we have a few anonymized case studies; I'll share a short writeup. it includes an on-prem agent install path.
[10:16] Tom Alvarez: ok good.
[10:18] Owen Patel: for the network checklist, add NAT egress cost estimates — we need to evaluate cloud egress impact.
[10:23] Lena Park: will do.
[10:25] Sara Kim: regarding audit logs, we need immutable logs for 1 year. is that an add-on?
[10:30] Riley Chen: extended audit retention is an add-on; we'll include pricing.
[10:33] Dr. Nina Rao: great, thanks.
[10:35] Lena Park: wrapping up — we'll: 1) send contract draft and blended pricing (Lena), 2) Marcus will send benchmark plan and provision dev cluster, 3) Owen will share infra diagram, 4) Sara will send compliance checklist. we'll reconvene after benchmark results. any final notes?
[10:54] Tom Alvarez: no, that covers it. thanks everyone.
[11:00] Lena Park: thanks, bye.
questions: What are the exact p99 latency targets for EU user flows?
Can Redwood integrate with Mantle's HSM-backed KMS for key control?
What's the estimated time-to-production for a hybrid Dedicated+Private deployment?
